Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, MARVEX combines real NASA planetary imagery with intelligent route planning, terrain analysis, resource management, and simulated emergency scenarios. Users can explore Martian locations, plan astronaut missions, compare alternative routes, and manage essential survival resources such as oxygen, battery power, and mission time.

The project addresses a critical challenge in Martian exploration: navigating unfamiliar terrain while dealing with limited resources, environmental hazards, and incomplete scientific information. Unlike conventional mapping platforms, MARVEX emphasizes uncertainty-aware decision-making, helping users understand why the shortest route may not always be the safest.

With Google Gemini AI integration, MARVEX aims to provide intelligent mission assistance and accessible scientific explanations.

By combining NASA data, AI, and interactive simulations, MARVEX makes planetary science engaging and accessible while demonstrating the importance of informed decision-making in future human exploration of Mars.
details:
MARVEX – Martian Exploration & Survival Intelligence

Explore Beyond the Known.

Project Overview

MARVEX (Martian Exploration & Survival Intelligence) is an AI-powered, interactive web application designed to simulate the challenges of exploring and surviving on Mars. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, MARVEX transforms NASA planetary observations into an engaging mission-planning and educational experience.

Our project addresses a fundamental challenge of future human exploration on Mars: How can astronauts navigate unfamiliar terrain, manage limited resources, and make informed decisions when scientific information is incomplete?

MARVEX combines Martian maps, terrain analysis, intelligent route planning, survival simulations, and AI-powered assistance into a unified platform.

How MARVEX Works

1. Interactive Mars Exploration

Users can explore Martian locations, including Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, and Eberswalde Crater, through an interactive interface featuring NASA planetary imagery.

Each destination provides geographical information, scientific context, and mission objectives.

2. Intelligent Route Planning

MARVEX allows users to plan exploration routes between a simulated astronaut habitat and scientific destinations.

The route-planning system is designed to consider distance, terrain conditions, potential hazards, and the availability of scientific observations.

Instead of simply identifying the shortest path, MARVEX encourages users to compare alternative routes and evaluate their potential risks.

3. Terrain Analysis and Uncertainty Awareness

One of MARVEX's most important innovations is its emphasis on uncertainty-aware exploration.

Some Martian regions have limited terrain observations. MARVEX is designed to highlight these areas and encourage users to investigate uncertain terrain before making important mission decisions.

Through simulated reconnaissance, users can discover how additional scientific information may change their original route.

4. Astronaut Survival and Resource Management

MARVEX incorporates educational simulations of essential mission resources, including:

  • Oxygen consumption
  • Battery and energy usage
  • Mission duration
  • Travel distance
  • Resource reserves

Users can explore how different routes and mission decisions affect their available resources.

These calculations use educational simulation assumptions rather than actual astronaut equipment specifications.

5. Emergency Mission Simulation

MARVEX is designed to introduce unexpected situations, such as increased energy consumption or equipment problems.

Users must evaluate their remaining resources and decide whether to continue exploring, reduce scientific activities, or return to their habitat.

This demonstrates the importance of adaptability and risk management during space exploration.

6. Gemini AI Mission Assistant

MARVEX incorporates Google Gemini AI into its mission-assistance concept.

The assistant is designed to explain terrain information, compare exploration routes, answer scientific questions, and help users understand simulated mission conditions.

An important design principle is separating numerical calculations from AI-generated explanations. The simulation engine handles resource calculations, while Gemini interprets the results in understandable language.

7. Mission Reports and Analysis

MARVEX is designed to generate mission summaries containing selected routes, resource consumption, emergency events, mission outcomes, and lessons learned.

This helps users understand how their decisions influenced the simulated exploration.

Technologies and Development Tools

MARVEX's proposed technology architecture includes:

Frontend Development

  • Next.js and React for the web application.
  • TypeScript for application logic.
  • Tailwind CSS for responsive interface design.
  • Three.js and React Three Fiber for interactive 3D visualizations.
  • MapLibre GL or Leaflet for planetary mapping.
  • Recharts for resource visualization.

Backend and Scientific Processing

  • Python for preparing NASA scientific datasets.
  • NumPy and Pandas for numerical and structured data processing.
  • GDAL and Rasterio for processing planetary terrain information.
  • A* pathfinding for calculating alternative routes.
  • TypeScript for educational mission simulations.

Artificial Intelligence

  • Google Gemini API for intelligent mission assistance and scientific explanations.

NASA Scientific Resources

  • Mars Odyssey THEMIS imagery.
  • Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) elevation data.
  • HiRISE imagery and terrain models.
  • Additional NASA planetary observations where suitable.

Development and Deployment

  • GitHub for source code management.
  • Vercel for planned web deployment.

These technologies form the proposed architecture; the final implementation may use a subset of them.

What Makes MARVEX Creative?

MARVEX goes beyond conventional Mars mapping by combining scientific exploration with interactive decision-making.

Our central innovation is that the shortest route is not always the safest route.

A shorter path may cross poorly understood terrain, while a longer route may provide more reliable information and better resource reserves.

MARVEX introduces a learning experience where users can investigate uncertain areas, compare alternatives, and observe how additional scientific evidence changes mission decisions.

By integrating NASA imagery, educational survival simulations, and AI-powered explanations, MARVEX connects scientific information with practical problem-solving.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team focused on several important considerations:

  1. Scientific Reliability: Distinguishing genuine NASA observations from simulated mission conditions.
  2. User Accessibility: Making complex planetary science understandable to students and beginners.
  3. Resource Limitations: Demonstrating the importance of oxygen, energy, and mission-time constraints.
  4. Terrain Uncertainty: Helping users understand the risks of making decisions with incomplete information.
  5. AI Accuracy: Keeping numerical calculations separate from AI-generated explanations.
  6. Performance and Scalability: Designing a browser-based platform that can support additional Martian locations and simulations.
  7. Educational Value: Encouraging experimentation, critical thinking, and scientific curiosity.

Benefits and Intended Impact

MARVEX aims to make Mars exploration more accessible, interactive, and educational.

For students, it provides an opportunity to learn about planetary science, geography, artificial intelligence, and engineering through practical simulations.

For educators, it offers a concept for demonstrating scientific decision-making, resource management, and risk assessment.

For space enthusiasts, it creates an engaging environment for exploring real Martian locations and understanding the challenges of future human missions.

The project also highlights the importance of scientific observations and reliable information when planning exploration activities.

MARVEX is an educational simulation, not a validated astronaut navigation or life-support system.

Conclusion

MARVEX transforms NASA's Martian observations into an interactive exploration and survival intelligence experience.

By combining real planetary imagery, terrain analysis, route planning, simulated resource management, emergency decision-making, and AI assistance, MARVEX demonstrates how scientific information can support better exploration decisions.

Our vision is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers while making the challenges of future Mars missions understandable to everyone.

MARVEX – Explore Beyond the Known.
